{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABitNeiw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhMD3Ew", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 260, "title": "Support persistent Saturn backup memory, battery state and 1 MiB/4 MiB RAM cartridges", "body": "## Problem

The Saturn player currently has a 32 KiB internal battery-backed RAM device, a deterministic SMPC RTC and four-byte SMEM, but they are not preserved across browser sessions. The only browser save-retention workflow is manual raw backup RAM import/export. The external cartridge slot does not yet implement the official Power Memory backup cartridge or the 1 MiB and 4 MiB expansion RAM cartridges.

The requester wants these related capabilities implemented together, including practical save management in the browser and authentic guest-visible cartridge hardware, so games can save normally and use the expansion memory they require.

## Expected outcome

Implement the following as **one complete task**, with a shared native/Wasm hardware model and a minimal browser UI consistent with the player redesign (#257/#258).

| Device | Capacity | Retention / purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Internal backup RAM | 32 KiB (256 Kbit) | Shared console-wide persistent game saves |
| Official Power Memory backup cartridge | 512 KiB (4 Mbit) | Independent persistent external game saves |
| 1 MiB expansion RAM cartridge | 1 MiB | Volatile game working memory |
| 4 MiB expansion RAM cartridge | 4 MiB | Volatile game working memory |
| SMPC battery state | RTC and documented SMEM/flags | Retain calendar, clock-setting state and console settings across sessions |

### Cartridge hardware

- Implement an exclusive virtual cartridge slot with **None**, **Backup Memory (512 KiB)**, **Expansion RAM (1 MiB)** and **Expansion RAM (4 MiB)**. Default to None for an untouched configuration. Internal backup RAM is present independently of the slot. A backup cartridge and an expansion cartridge cannot be simultaneously installed.
- Research the actual Saturn A-bus CS0/CS1/CS2 address decoding, official cartridge IDs, chip capacity/bank layout, mirrors/holes, bus widths and lanes, read/write restrictions, absence behavior, cache aliases, bus waits and relevant reset domains. Compare primary Sega documentation and well-established emulator implementations (e.g. Mednafen, Yabause, Ymir) as corroborating evidence; document unresolved hardware behavior and bounded compatibility choices. Do not simply map a contiguous arbitrary array or invent a cartridge ID.
- Route guest accesses through the ordinary shared CPU/bus/DMA/device model. Preserve big-endian values, access ordering, arbitration and timing in exact and normal relaxed playback; no per-game patches, host-written guest acknowledgements or separate browser-only RAM simulation. Ensure real guest code can identify, read and write the correct cartridge and use legitimate transfer paths.
- Model expansion RAM as volatile; distinguish power-cycle, system reset, manual CPU reset and cartridge replacement according to evidence. Do not serialize expansion RAM as battery-backed saves. Explicit cartridge changes must stop playback/release input and take effect at a safe cold-boot boundary; retain accepted disc, BIOS and battery-backed bytes. Do not simulate unsupported live hot-plug.
- Support firmware and HLE boot. Extend the original guest-executed HLE BUP library so documented external backup device discovery, partitions, capacity/status, formatting, directory, file read/write/delete/verify and error behavior work when the backup cartridge is present and report absence when it is not. Preserve the existing internal-device and ABI contracts. Expansion RAM is not a backup-library storage device.

### Persistent battery-backed storage and RTC

- Use local, origin-scoped IndexedDB for the shared console's internal 32 KiB backup image, the independent external 512 KiB backup image and validated SMPC battery state. They must not be keyed by individual game, disc or BIOS; ordinary media changes must not erase or replace the console's saved state. Remember the selected virtual cartridge locally if useful, separately from memory data.
- Restore accepted persisted state **before** first guest execution or boot that can modify it. Track actual dirty changes, use bounded coalesced asynchronous writes and explicit flush/acknowledgement semantics for pause/reset/media or cartridge transitions, tab hiding and shutdown where feasible. Avoid repeated full snapshots or synchronous storage work on the per-field hot path. Do not promise that an abrupt browser/process kill can always flush the last outstanding write.
- Preserve correct RTC/SMEM reset retention. For browser battery-backed time, record a validated guest clock/calendar offset or battery snapshot with a host time anchor, and advance by elapsed offline time with defined behavior for clock rollback, invalid data and date rollover. Preserve a deterministic, injectable time contract for native/Wasm tests; do not introduce nondeterministic host time inside the core scheduler. Never silently overwrite guest SETTIME/SETSMEM settings with a host wall-clock value.
- Handle missing records, unavailable storage, permission errors, quota/write failure, corrupted/unsupported records, interrupted transactions, stale asynchronous results and simultaneous tabs safely. Clearly distinguish empty storage from failed restore; do not replace unreadable existing saves with zeroes. Keep the current in-memory state recoverable and exportable; provide retry/recovery and prevent a conflicting stale writer or destructive transition from silently overwriting newer saves. Make durability/status claims only after acknowledged storage commits. Prefer a small versioned storage contract and use transactions/ownership or equivalent safe conflict detection.
- Update the existing privacy contract explicitly: only battery-backed state and relevant player preferences may be stored locally; no automatic storage of BIOS, disc images, game ROMs, traces, expansion RAM or save states, no upload/network sync/analytics. Explain origin/browser storage limits and that clearing site data can erase saves.

### Save management and format compatibility

- Provide a compact cartridge selector and a Save management area in the existing player/Advanced UI. Show internal memory and the external backup cartridge as distinct devices, with capacity, persistence status and accessible import/export actions. Preserve the existing 32768-byte packed raw internal import/export contract; add a documented raw external cartridge image contract. External saves must remain available when switching to an expansion cartridge or None.
- Support explicit formatting/clearing of each backup device with a clear destructive-action warning/confirmation (ordinary in-product consent, **not a human acceptance or closure gate**). Pause at a safe boundary, validate data before mutation, allow recovery/export and avoid implicit formatting or silent deletion. A failed or cancelled import must not change accepted memory or persisted data. Prefer the guest's ordinary backup-library or genuine firmware memory manager for per-file operations rather than implementing a duplicate host filesystem editor unless needed for the specified management behavior.
- Existing HLE uses the independently implemented SRBUP001 filesystem; it is not the genuine Sega BIOS physical backup format. Investigate documented and independently corroborated Saturn backup filesystem layouts and interoperability. Aim for a shared authentic format where sufficiently established, with independently authored code and fixtures. If the evidence does not establish a safe shared format, retain an explicitly identified compatible HLE format and clearly document the limitations; do not mislabel it as a genuine Sega save or silently reinterpret/format raw imported BIOS data. Preserve existing SRBUP001 and raw imports byte-for-byte unless an explicitly requested, validated migration/format operation is performed. If migration is offered, test rollback and data preservation. Genuine BIOS mode must continue executing the supplied firmware against the real emulated storage devices; no host fake BIOS memory manager.
- Ensure the UI remains simple, responsive and accessible; no second startup wizard, duplicate boot choice or per-game automatic cartridge switch. Retain auto BIOS/HLE selection, current CRT/touch/gamepad/audio/fullscreen/Debug functionality, and the user's ability to manage saves without exposing unrelated diagnostics.

## Context and reproduction

Inspected main: `232d077c041211d7d037fa117a8c1712d59f63b5` (PR #259). The baseline already has:
- `src/backup.rs`: packed 32 KiB battery RAM on odd byte lanes with address mirrors, atomic raw import, retained through volatile resets.
- `src/smpc.rs`: deterministic BCD Gregorian RTC, SETTIME/SETSMEM, four-byte battery memory and reset retention.
- `src/hle/backup.s`, [HLE documentation](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/src/hle/README.md#independent-backup-library), and original BUP ABI fixture/tests: internal device 0 only, optional devices absent, independent SRBUP001 format. Unknown raw imports are retained until explicit guest Format.
- `src/bus.rs`, native machine, Wasm exports, `web/worker-emulator.js` and playback Worker/client, `web/app.js`, `web/index.html`: existing shared bus, Worker state/lifecycle, local raw backup import/export. The current UI warns that closing or reloading loses the in-memory copy.

Reproduce the persistence gap using an original backup guest: save, reload without exporting/importing, and observe the fresh internal RAM; insert no cartridge (the current only configuration) and observe optional device absence. Existing backup/RTC and BUP fixtures should be reused and extended. Consult Sega SCU ST-097, SMPC ST-169, system/backup library ST-162-R1 and available cartridge hardware documentation, alongside independent emulator sources. Do not copy SDK/firmware objects, third-party emulator implementation code or proprietary saves/ROMs.

Related to #17; this increment does not complete the umbrella hardware tracker or the #138 real-time goal.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

**All mandatory checks must be executable and verifiable by the implementation agent before merge. Do not require human confirmation, physical hardware, personal BIOS/game dumps, subjective review of the UI, manual gameplay or live Pages verification for Issue closure.** Follow the repository's development flow and UI/UX/CI principles.

- [ ] **Evidence and device decoding:** document primary source sections, corroborating implementations, cartridge identification and exact supported mappings/capacity/lane/mirror/reset/timing rules. Native tests and original SH-2 guests distinguish absent slot, backup, 1 MiB and 4 MiB cartridges; exercise endpoints, aliases, holes, byte/word/long accesses, both CPUs, allowed DMA paths and non-aliasing with other devices. Verify ordinary hardware paths, including exact vs relaxed where applicable, rather than host-only arrays.
- [ ] **Real save services:** original BIOS-path reset-vector and HLE guests exercise internal and external backup storage and actual guest-visible detection. Extend original BUP tests for both devices, capacity/full/absent/invalid cases, partitions, format, write/read/directory/delete/verify, corruption bounds and reset retention. Preserve existing ABI and internal fixtures. Document and test the selected format compatibility policy, including safe handling of unknown/legacy/raw images and explicit format/migration if supported. Never require genuine proprietary firmware or a private save dump.
- [ ] **Reset and slot lifecycle:** prove that internal and external saved bytes are independent and survive applicable reset, boot-mode and slot changes. Volatile expansion RAM has evidence-backed reset/replacement behavior and is never persisted as save data. Switching slot is safe, exclusive, retains media and does not unexpectedly resume playback or overwrite backup data.
- [ ] **Durable browser saves:** production Wasm/Chromium tests write actual guest saves and acknowledge commits, reload in the same origin, restore before guest execution and verify all bytes and guest-visible records for both devices. Cover multiple games/BIOS paths sharing the same console storage; switch cartridges and return to Power Memory without data loss; test fresh origin, browser-storage clear and reload semantics. Confirm no per-game backup duplication.
- [ ] **RTC and settings retention:** original guests exercise SETTIME/SETSMEM and subsequent INTBACK across reset and restored sessions; injected host clock tests cover elapsed offline time, midnight/month/leap-day/year rollover, clock rollback and invalid snapshot handling. Preserve deterministic existing native timing and date validation.
- [ ] **Failure safety:** automated storage failure injection covers initial read failure, corruption, unsupported versions, write/quota errors, interrupted/stale operations, competing tabs and retry. Failed restores/imports never format or overwrite unknown bytes; failed saves retain recoverable RAM and report unsaved status. Explicit raw imports/exports round-trip both devices byte-for-byte, including invalid size and asynchronous cancellation; destructive formatting requires explicit in-product confirmation. Demonstrate negative controls where useful.
- [ ] **UI/UX and privacy:** verify selector, capacity/labels, pending/ready/error states, save management, confirmation/cancellation, focus, keyboard and responsive layouts with browser automation. No human approval or real device tests. Verify no BIOS/disc persistence, upload, external requests or hidden game downloads. Keep current boot, player, touch/gamepad, CRT, audio and Advanced/Debug paths working.
- [ ] **Performance and regression:** preserve existing bus timing and Worker ownership, bounded storage queues and frame/audio delivery; no unnecessary per-frame storage reads/writes or large copies. Measure a bounded original-guest normal-playback comparison and document performance/memory overhead; do not require a host-specific FPS threshold. Run applicable native locked build/tests/Clippy, fixture reproduction, production compatible/accelerated Wasm builds, complete browser groups and runner/artifact checks according to the repository tooling. Add focused regressions rather than duplicating expensive suites, preserve existing hardware oracles, and require passing applicable exact-head PR CI. Update README, setup, architecture/conformance, HLE-format and validation documentation. Merge and close only after the entire scoped hardware, persistence and UI implementation is complete.

## Optional validation

None required for closure. A user may later try their own lawfully obtained firmware, games and real-cartridge backup files, but these are not required deliverables or blockers.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Do not keep this Issue open pending human testing or deployment checks.
